evidence: Opened only: the brief, GATE-INPUTS.json, HUMANIZATION-TELL-INVENTORY.md, and G-S36's DRAFT.txt, CONTEXT.txt and SOURCE.txt; I read ADMISSION.json only after forming my own view. DRAFT judged: 'What’s theirs and what’s mine?' (one question, two curly apostrophes). CHANGE: matches the_change. In CONTEXT it appears once, as the fifth of seven questions in the last paragraph ('What actually happened? What was the impact? What boundaries need to be set? What shaped the other person(s) into someone capable of that harm? What’s theirs and what’s mine? What does accountability require? How can I let this go, without denying any of the above?'), where 'What is theirs? What is mine?' stood; the neighbouring 'What boundaries need to be set?' is the working copy's wording and Emulate's failed 'What boundaries do I need to set as a result?' is not there, as the_change requires. MEANING: SOURCE keeps his 'What belongs to them?' / 'What belongs to me?'. The draft asks those same two things, what is the other person's and what is mine, as one question. It adds no claim, fact, name or example and drops no point; the words it replaces already had no quote marks, so none are lost by the swap. READS IN CONTEXT: 'theirs' points to 'the other person(s)' in the question immediately before it (the writer's C02 note says 'two before'; it is the next one back, so the pronoun is closer than claimed, which is not a problem); 'mine' is the asker and matches the 'I' of the last question; the question follows naturally from 'What shaped the other person(s) into someone capable of that harm?' as the next thing to sort out. The contraction fits the section's own (doesn’t, don’t, we’re, you’re, won’t), both apostrophes are curly like the section's, and lower-case 'what’s' after 'and' is correct. TELLS: PRESENT, inherited and justified: T02. The last paragraph is a run of short questions that each do one job in order, so the cadence is there at paragraph scale and I disagree with the writer's ledger saying ABSENT; but it is the working copy's own list (a list of questions alone is not the tell), the swap touches one item, and joining two questions into one makes the run a beat shorter, not longer. Considered and not flagged: T12 (theirs/mine is a matched pair, but it is the question itself and his published pair, a naturally necessary contrast the inventory exempts; the join with 'and' adds no polish); T06 ('theirs' and 'mine' are as general as his 'belongs to them / belongs to me', in a list of prompts, not abstraction standing in for something concrete); T09 and T13, which the linter points to (the run varies in weight, from the short 'What was the impact?' to the long 'What shaped the other person(s)...' and a last question whose 'without denying any of the above' calls back to the lead-in's 'while still holding all of the above'; the section has hedges, asides and a quoted script; the swap removes none of it); T14 (nothing reordered, cut or moved: the question keeps its place); T15 (a contraction and a join of the same two words, not a swap for less likely ones); T20 and T29 (it is mid-paragraph, not the closing line); T26 (the repeated 'what’s' is the pair's own parallelism, and the 'What' openers are the grammar of the list). The T10-style phrases elsewhere in the section ('You don’t have to forgive before you’re ready', 'we don’t have to forgive first') are not in the draft and are not touched by it. Every other row (T01, T03 to T05, T07, T08, T11, T16 to T19, T21 to T25, T27, T28, C01 to C04) is absent in the draft; C03 and C04: no first-person fact and no sourced claim added. LINTER: 'B7 short landing at paragraph end' flagged the draft because the linter saw it alone; in CONTEXT two questions follow it ('What does accountability require?' and 'How can I let this go, without denying any of the above?'), so it is not the paragraph's end: accepted. 'D9 follows the source order' (1/1 paragraphs, agreement 1.00): an in-place swap of one question in a list cannot reorder anything, and its pointer to T13 and T09 is answered above: accepted.
